paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table, recorded as one entry per the pass instructions. The en field is identical to the zh field: every cell is a chemical symbol or a compound number, and the only German-language token on the page is the column head 'Nr.' (Nummer, i.e. No.), which is left as printed so the header row matches the source. The table continues from the preceding page: it opens mid-sequence at Nr. 499 with no Tabelle caption on this page, so the shared substituents that caption fixes and the scaffold it draws are not visible here and are not reproduced. The column heads are printed with superscripts, R with a raised 1, 2 and 3; they are transcribed inline as R1, R2, R3. Likewise the subscript digits in OCH2CH2F, OCH2CH2Br, SO2Me, SO2Et and CF3 are printed as true subscripts and transcribed inline. The header row is set on a grey stippled ground; that is print shading, not content. A small ink blot sits in the R3 cell of Nr. 500, well to the right of the printed SO2Et and not touching it; it reads as a scan artifact rather than a character, and the cell value is fully legible. Faint stray dots sit in the left margin beside the header line and beside the Nr. cell of 512, and in the blank lower half of the page; these are also scan artifacts. The table body ends after Nr. 516 and the lower half of the page is blank. The page carries no footer.
